1.stem: The student wants to note a limitation a cautious reader should keep in mind. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: The exposure levels used in the study matched the concentrations that bees actually encounter in real agricultural fields.
options.B: The study's reach was narrow: it lasted a single season, covered only one region of France, and tested only honeybees.
options.C: Colonies exposed to the pesticide lost 30% more workers over the foraging season than the unexposed control colonies did over the same period.
options.D: The colonies exposed to the pesticide were compared against a group of unexposed control colonies.

2.stem: The student wants to point out an exception to the general migratory pattern. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Although most of the studied warblers migrated south by October, the yellow-rumped warbler remained in the north through the winter.
options.B: Most of the twelve warbler species in the study had migrated south by October, departing in flocks once the northern nights turned cold.
options.C: The warbler species that did migrate departed in flocks rather than singly, a habit the study recorded throughout the whole of the autumn season.
options.D: The blackpoll warbler flew a nonstop three-day route across the Atlantic, an unusually demanding crossing for a bird weighing barely twelve grams.

3.stem: The student wants to acknowledge a drawback of electric buses while still supporting the conclusion that the switch was worthwhile. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: The battery range of an electric bus drops by about 20 percent in cold winter weather, a problem the city has had to plan around every year since it made the switch in 2021.
options.B: Although electric buses cost about 40% more to buy than diesel buses, lower fuel and maintenance costs offset that premium over 12 years, making the switch worthwhile.
options.C: In 2021, the city replaced 100 diesel buses with electric ones, which cut pollution along their routes by about 60 percent.
options.D: Electric buses cut air pollution along the routes they serve by about 60 percent, a marked improvement over the 100 diesel buses the city retired when it made the switch in 2021.

4.stem: The student wants to draw a single general conclusion supported by all three studies. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: In the 2020 study, nurses working night shifts scored lower on memory tests than the colleagues who worked the day shift on the same wards.
options.B: A 2021 study found that a nap taken soon after learning improved later recall in older adults.
options.C: In the 2019 study, students who slept eight hours recalled 25 percent more words than students who had been kept awake the night before.
options.D: Across several different populations and tasks, adequate sleep was consistently associated with better memory performance.

5.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

options.A: Meanwhile,
options.B: Nevertheless,
options.C: Instead,
options.D: Likewise,

6.stem: The student wants to caution readers against concluding that coffee shops cause higher incomes. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: The data cannot show that coffee shops raise incomes; the shops simply tend to open in areas that are already affluent.
options.B: The link between coffee shops and higher average incomes held consistently across all 100 cities studied.
options.C: The income figures behind the analysis came from census records collected for all 100 cities.
options.D: Across the 100 cities in the study, those with the most coffee shops reported higher average incomes than those with the fewest.

7.stem: The student wants to present the study's central result to a skeptical reader while making clear that the finding is only preliminary. Which choice best accomplishes this goal?

options.A: In a single, not-yet-replicated greenhouse trial, treated tomato plants grew 18% taller than untreated ones—a promising but preliminary result.
options.B: Field conditions differ from greenhouse conditions in temperature and soil variability, and the researchers have not yet repeated the trial under either set of conditions.
options.C: Tomato plants treated with Bacillus subtilis strain X grew 18% taller than untreated plants, a gain that points to the growth-promoting hormones it may produce.
options.D: The bacterium, Bacillus subtilis strain X, may produce hormones that promote growth in the tomato plants treated with it.

8.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

options.A: Hence,
options.B: Likewise,
options.C: Namely,
options.D: That said,

9.stem: The student wants to highlight a surprising disconnect between how alert the 6-hour sleepers felt and how they actually performed. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Though the 6-hour sleepers rated themselves as alert as the 8-hour group, their reaction times were as slow as those of people kept awake for 24 hours.
options.B: The study followed 48 healthy adults over 14 nights.
options.C: The 8-hour sleepers maintained stable reaction times throughout the study.
options.D: On reaction-time tests, the 6-hour sleepers performed as poorly as people who had stayed awake for 24 hours straight.

10.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

options.A: By contrast,
options.B: Instead,
options.C: Finally,
options.D: What is more,

11.stem: The student wants to emphasize a contrast between the findings of the two studies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Study A, which surveyed 200 college students about their sleep habits, found that those sleeping 8 hours scored higher on memory tests.
options.B: Both Study A and Study B were published in peer-reviewed journals, one surveying college students and the other adults in ten countries.
options.C: Whereas Study A linked 8 hours of sleep to better memory scores, Study B found no connection between sleep duration and memory.
options.D: Study B surveyed 5,000 adults across ten different countries, a far larger and more varied sample than the 200 college students of Study A.

15.stem: The student wants to present a cautious summary of the findings. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Vidal's mapping suggests that flowering roadside verges may carry roughly 1.9 times the bee traffic of comparable routes without them, though a single summer of survey data leaves the pattern unconfirmed.
options.B: Vidal's mapping suggests that canal-bank plantings may carry roughly 2.5 times the bee traffic of comparable routes without them, though a sample of just 14 of some 60 corridors leaves the pattern unconfirmed.
options.C: Vidal's mapping suggests that rooftop gardens may carry roughly 2.8 times the bee traffic of comparable routes without them, though volunteer counts never checked by a trained observer leave the pattern unconfirmed.
options.D: Vidal's mapping suggests that unmowed vacant lots may carry roughly 2.2 times the bee traffic of comparable routes without them, though reliable identification of only one bee genus leaves the pattern unconfirmed.

16.stem: The student wants to compare the results of the two conditions. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Ollila's lubricated curves ran 7 decibels quieter than the untreated curves, which also wore their rail flanges 2.2 times as fast.
options.B: Ollila's lubricated curves ran 11 decibels quieter than the untreated curves, which also wore their rail flanges 2.9 times as fast.
options.C: Ollila's lubricated curves ran 9 decibels quieter than the untreated curves, which also wore their rail flanges 1.1 times as fast.
options.D: Ollila's lubricated curves ran 13 decibels quieter than the untreated curves, which also wore their rail flanges 1.6 times as fast.

17.stem: The student wants to emphasize the battery's advantage for large-scale grid energy storage specifically. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Because sodium is cheap and abundant, the new battery could make large-scale grid energy storage far cheaper.
options.B: The new battery holds less energy per kilogram than a lithium-ion battery, so it is heavier for the amount of charge it can store.
options.C: The new sodium-ion battery performs better in cold weather than a lithium-ion battery does, holding its charge as temperatures fall.
options.D: Sodium is far cheaper and more abundant than lithium, which is why the researchers built their new battery around it.

20.stem: The student wants to emphasize the study's main finding. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Okonkwo's central finding is that chute damage comes down to bin lining: libraries that softened the bin's lining cut damaged returns by 71 percent.
options.B: Okonkwo's central finding is that chute damage comes down to drop height: libraries that lowered the drop into the collection bin cut damaged returns by 62 percent.
options.C: Okonkwo's central finding is that chute damage comes down to emptying interval: libraries that emptied their bins more often cut damaged returns by 53 percent.
options.D: Okonkwo's central finding is that chute damage comes down to belt speed: libraries that slowed the chute's conveyor belt cut damaged returns by 44 percent.

21.stem: The student wants to compare the results of the two conditions. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Over the nine-month trial the strips behind the filmed windows lost 26 percent of their original color intensity, while the strips behind the untreated windows lost 31 percent.
options.B: Over the nine-month trial the strips behind the filmed windows lost 19 percent of their original color intensity, while the strips behind the untreated windows lost 58 percent.
options.C: Over the nine-month trial the strips behind the filmed windows lost 12 percent of their original color intensity, while the strips behind the untreated windows lost 45 percent.
options.D: Over the nine-month trial the strips behind the filmed windows lost 34 percent of their original color intensity, while the strips behind the untreated windows lost 49 percent.

22.stem: The student wants to emphasize that two independent methods corroborated the artifact's age. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Radiocarbon dating, which measures the decay of carbon-14, placed the artifact at about 1200 CE, whereas thermoluminescence dating instead measures the electrons trapped in fired clay.
options.B: Thermoluminescence dating works by measuring the electrons that become trapped in fired clay, a physical principle entirely different from the radioactive decay that radiocarbon dating measures.
options.C: Though radiocarbon and thermoluminescence rely on entirely different physical principles, they dated the artifact within two decades of each other—about 1200 and 1180 CE.
options.D: The two dating methods rely on entirely different physical principles, so neither of them depends on the assumptions made by the other.
